summary: Piscataquis County, Maine, lookout on the Appalachian Trail, built 1906 and steel by 1921; removed 1993, with a rock pile, debris and a radio site left on the summit.

facts.design: Steel tower on an 18-foot quadripod, topped by an 8-foot square white cabin (1955 survey description)
facts.status_note: Removed in 1993; a rock pile marks the site and remnants are scattered in the trees, per a 2011 trip report and the willhiteweb history

access.note: Summit reached on foot along the Appalachian Trail; a 2011 trip report describes parking outside a gate on the Frenchtown road and walking to the trailhead

visit.trail_note: Hike the Appalachian Trail to the summit; the 2011 trip report describes parking outside a gate and walking to the trailhead

Tower removed; part of the tower foot remains in a rock pile at the summit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Maine Memory caption (wood tower rebuilt 1940, replaced 1920) is out of order and conflicts with the detailed timeline that has the steel tower started 1920 and completed 1921; the story follows the detailed timeline.
Maine Memory gives the lookout as 3,707 feet and willhiteweb gives elevation as 3,654 feet; the story gives neither figure.

sources.title: White Cap Mountain fire lookout camp, ca. 1920
Fire lookout station, White Cap Mountain, ca. 1920

notes_for_editor: No source explains why the tower was removed in 1993, so the story gives no reason. The willhiteweb page carries photos (credits include Bill Spach; captions cite 1934, 1955 and 1978) but no image URLs appeared in the cached text, so none are recorded. The guessed NHLR URL is not in the cache. The 2011 trip report is a forum post; treat its gate description as a 2011 observation. Brief status 'gone' and the 1993 removal are confirmed by two sources.
